Derivative directions of cppFUN()

Source: vignettes/articles/methods-cppfun.Rmd
methods-cppfun.Rmd

Here \(x\) denotes the variables of the function, not ODE states; other symbols are those of the notation table. R interface: cppFUN() and evaluateMany().

cppFUN() compiles an algebraic system \[ y_i = g_i(x_1, \dots, x_{n_x}, p_1, \dots, p_{n_p}), \qquad i = 1, \dots, n_y, \tag{1} \] with the first and second derivatives of \(g\), named as the derivatives of solveODE(). The variables \(x\) are the rows of an \(n_{\mathrm{obs}} \times n_x\) matrix, one per observation; the parameters \(p\) are shared by all rows. Typical uses: observation maps and reparametrizations \((x_0, p) = \Phi(\theta)\), the Jacobian being the tangent of Forward (2).

From the expression graph the generator emits two templates over the scalar type:

  • \(g\) for one observation, instantiated on double, cppde::dual<double> and the nested cppde::dual2nd<double>;
  • the vector-Jacobian product as a reverse sweep on the same graph, instantiated on double and the dual.

With the default compile = FALSE the constructor only writes the source, and the functions stop with an error until compile().

Entry points and derivative directions

derivMode names the products built, any of "forward" (default), "reverse" and "forward-reverse" (implies "reverse"); a product left out costs no entries and no compile time. deriv and deriv2 switch the first- and second-order entries; deriv2 = TRUE requires "forward".

R functions and compiled entries, prefixed by the model name; x, p stand for vars, params. _c entries are .Call interfaces taking arguments by reference; .C versions of _eval, _eval_ad, _eval_ad2 and _vjp serve a shared object without the .Call symbol. Under "forward-reverse", _vjp_ad is also a thread-safe plain C entry.
R function direction compiled entry
func(x, p) any _eval_c
jac(x, p[, tangentX, tangentP]) forward _eval_ad_c
hess(x, p[, tangentX, tangentP, hessianX, hessianP]) forward _eval_ad2_c
evaluate(..., deriv2) forward _eval_ad_c or _eval_ad2_c
evaluateBatch(sets, cores, deriv2) forward _eval_ad_batch or _eval_ad2_batch
vjp(x, p, cotangent) reverse _vjp_c
vjp(x, p, cotangent, tangentX, tangentP, curvature) forward-reverse _vjp_ad_c

Forward direction. jac evaluates \(g\) on duals, hess on nested duals; they return arrays \([n_{\mathrm{obs}}, n_y, M]\) and \([n_{\mathrm{obs}}, n_y, M, M]\). Tangents (next section) set the directions \(\theta \in \mathbb{R}^M\), by default the identity over the variables and differentiated parameters. evaluate returns y, tangent and, with deriv2 = TRUE, hessian from one pass instead of up to three. evaluateBatch runs evaluate over a list of argument sets on OpenMP threads with dynamic scheduling, as a loop for fewer than two sets. evaluateMany() does the same for one argument set each of several cppFUN() objects, in one parallel region.

Reverse direction. For a cotangent \(w\) of the outputs, \([n_{\mathrm{obs}}, n_y]\) or \([n_{\mathrm{obs}}, n_y, n_{\mathrm{seed}}]\), vjp returns the value \(y\) and \[ (w_x)_{o j s} = \sum_{i} w_{o i s}\, \frac{\partial g_i}{\partial x_j}(x_o, p), \qquad (w_p)_{k s} = \sum_{o} \sum_{i} w_{o i s}\, \frac{\partial g_i}{\partial p_k}(x_o, p), \tag{2} \] as cotangentX and cotangentP. The contraction is one reverse sweep per observation and cotangent column, at a cost independent of the number of upstream parameters, without forming Jacobian or Hessian. Statements independent of the cotangent run once per observation.

With input tangents \(v_x\), \(v_p\) in \(n_{\mathrm{dir}}\) directions (tangentX, tangentP) or the derivative \(\dot w\) of the cotangent along them (curvature), vjp runs the same template on duals and also returns \[ \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}v}\bigl(w^{\mathsf T} J\bigr) = w^{\mathsf T}\,\frac{\partial J}{\partial (x, p)}\,v + \dot w^{\mathsf T} J, \qquad J = \frac{\partial g}{\partial (x, p)}, \tag{3} \] as curvatureX and curvatureP, forward over reverse (second derivatives) without a Hessian.

Tangent, hessian, cotangent and curvature

The upstream map \(\Phi: \theta \mapsto (x, p)\) has the tangent \(\partial\Phi(\theta)\) and the hessian \(\partial^2\Phi(\theta)\). A scalar functional \(L\) of the outputs has the cotangent \(\partial L(y)\) and the curvature \(\partial^2 L(y)\,\partial y\), the derivative of the cotangent along the tangent. Forward arguments live on the inputs, reverse arguments on the outputs, results on the other side.

The four derivative objects in R. solveODE() uses one name for argument and result; cppFUN() results are elements of the lists from evaluate and vjp.
solveODE() cppFUN() argument cppFUN() result
tangent tangentX, tangentP tangent
hessian hessianX, hessianP hessian
cotangent cotangent cotangentX, cotangentP
curvature curvature curvatureX, curvatureP

Forward over forward maps input to output hessian in every pair of tangent directions. Forward over reverse maps output to input curvature, the Hessian of the seeded functional applied to the tangent; the identity tangent gives the Hessian columns.

Chain rule. Tangent and hessian of the inputs come in two blocks each:

  • tangentX[obs, name, theta]: \(\partial x_i/\partial\theta_a\), per observation row;
  • tangentP[name, theta]: \(\partial p_j/\partial\theta_a\), shared by all observations;
  • hessianX[obs, name, theta1, theta2]: \(\partial^2 x_i/\partial\theta_a\partial\theta_b\), optional, zero by default;
  • hessianP[name, theta1, theta2]: \(\partial^2 p_j/\partial\theta_a\partial\theta_b\), optional, zero by default.

Attributes deriv and deriv2 of variables and parameters are an alternative. Parameters in fixed and symbols absent from the tangent have zero tangent rows.

With the tangent \(\partial\Phi \in \mathbb{R}^{n_{\mathrm{obs}} \times n_{\mathrm{diff}} \times M}\) over the \(n_{\mathrm{diff}} = n_x + n_p\) inputs and the hessian \(\partial^2\Phi\), the chain rule gives the Jacobian \[ \frac{\partial y}{\partial\theta}\bigg|_{\mathrm{obs}} = J\bigl(x_{\mathrm{obs}}, p\bigr) \cdot \partial\Phi_{\mathrm{obs}}, \tag{4} \] and the Hessian of output \(i\) \[ \frac{\partial^2 y_i}{\partial\theta\,\partial\theta^{\mathsf T}}\bigg|_{\mathrm{obs}} = \partial\Phi_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\mathsf T} \, H_i\bigl(x_{\mathrm{obs}}, p\bigr) \, \partial\Phi_{\mathrm{obs}} + \sum_{j} J_{i, j}\bigl(x_{\mathrm{obs}}, p\bigr) \, \partial^2\Phi_{\mathrm{obs}, j, \cdot, \cdot}, \tag{5} \] whose second term vanishes for affine \(\Phi\). Neither \(J\) nor \(H\) is formed; seeding the dual tangent slots gives both contractions. Each input becomes \[ \tilde x_i = (x_i + \partial\Phi_{i,\cdot}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}) + \bigl(\partial\Phi_{i,\cdot} + \partial^2\Phi_{i,\cdot,\cdot}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}\bigr)\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}, \] a nested dual: inner tangents \(\partial x_i/\partial\theta\), outer slot \(k\) an inner dual with value \(\partial x_i/\partial\theta_k\) and inner tangents \(\partial^2 x_i/\partial\theta_k\partial\theta\). One evaluation propagates both terms of (5). The inner tangents of \(\tilde y\) are \(\partial y/\partial\theta\), the cross slots \(\tilde y[k][m]\) are \(\partial^2 y/\partial\theta_k\partial\theta_m\).

Pass-through of unmodeled inputs

With attach.input = TRUE, inputs that are not variables or parameters of (1) pass to the output unchanged: values copied, Jacobian rows zero for a variable and the identity for a parameter, Hessian rows zero. An observation map then need not repeat every integrator column as an identity, as with the partial-shape tangent of solveODE().
